22 The diagram shows a representation of a wave on the screen of an oscilloscope.
1 cm
The y-gain is set to 3.5 mV cm–1.
What is the amplitude of the wave?
A
0.57 mV
B
3.5 mV
C
7.0 mV
D
14 mV

hints: Look at the centre horizontal line of the trace and measure from there to the top of a crest, not from the bottom of the screen.
Count grid squares using the marked $1 \text{ cm}$ square height to find how many cm the peak is above equilibrium.
Multiply that amplitude in cm by the y-gain of $3.5 \text{ mV cm}^{-1}$ to convert screen height to voltage.
walkthrough: Identify equilibrium as the central horizontal line that the wave crosses. Amplitude is the maximum displacement from that line to a crest or trough.
Use the $1 \text{ cm}$ marker to calibrate the vertical scale. One vertical grid square is $1 \text{ cm}$.
Count from the centre line to a peak: the crest is $2$ squares above the centre, so amplitude height $= 2.0 \text{ cm}$. The full crest-to-trough height is $4.0 \text{ cm}$.
Calculate $2.0 \times 3.5 = 7.0$ with unit $\text{mV}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a large factor and does not match $2 \text{ cm} \times 3.5 \text{ mV cm}^{-1}$. It may come from incorrectly dividing instead of multiplying by the y-gain.

B.explanation: This is the voltage for only $1 \text{ cm}$ deflection. The amplitude from the centre line to a peak is $2 \text{ cm}$, not $1 \text{ cm}$.

C.explanation: Amplitude is $2 \text{ cm}$ from equilibrium to peak, so $2 \times 3.5 = 7.0 \text{ mV}$.

D.explanation: This is the peak-to-trough voltage for $4 \text{ cm}$. Amplitude is half the peak-to-trough height, so this is twice too large.
